analysis:
All changes are documentation only. No enforcement code was supplied, so the doc statements about code behavior are unverified.

prefix-cache.md (head lines ~130-153) adds an unregistered GLM sparse-state candidate. It describes GLM5NextPagedSparseState, PagedImmutableSnapshot copy-on-write, a new full-state codec layout, and default-on SSD eligibility for one GLM-5.3 model via isGLM5NextDefaultModel. DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 opts out. The codec claims to require a protected native binding and a verified encrypted restore path. Relevant to T-041 (SSD cache at-rest and TTFT oracle) and A-001. T-041 does not list the new codec or files, and it assumes a coordinator-authored cacheSalt, while GLM is stated to be outside the registered coordinator serving models. I recorded one low finding for this threat-model gap. The next pass should check the real PrefixCachePolicy, codec and store code for cacheSalt/tenant scoping, HMAC lookup tags, TTL and the KEK binding on the GLM path.

inference.md changes cover MiMo audio/video decode accounting, tool-schema restoration, memory charging and GLM tool-suffix validation. The doc says reserved schema metadata is rejected and that no tool, media or memory-admission bypass is granted. These are consistent with fail-closed behavior, but the underlying code was not supplied.

model-registry.md adds a raw GLM discovery quotation note. It states the quotation is not a download receipt and does not replace catalog/source identity or native validation. No security regression is evident from the text.

findings.detail: The new prefix-cache.md section says SSD eligibility defaults on for the locally selected EigenLabs/GLM-5.3-Flash-MLX-NVFP4-mtp (PrefixCachePolicy.isGLM5NextDefaultModel). It also adds a distinct on-disk layout, native-paged-glm5next-full-state-v1, which stores sparse latent, index-key, convolution/recurrence and MTP state. T-041 documents the SSD tier's at-rest and TTFT-oracle posture, its sign-off and its affected_files list, and none of these cover the new GLM codec or default-on activation. T-041's cacheSalt scoping assumes a coordinator-authored salt. The doc says GLM is outside the registered coordinator serving models, so the supplied text does not show what tenant scope, TTL, per-donation gating or KEK/HMAC lookup-tag binding apply on the local path. This is a documentation and threat-model gap, not a demonstrated vulnerability. Fix: add the GLM codec and policy files to T-041, state the cacheSalt source in local mode, and confirm that HMAC lookup tags, the 30-minute sliding TTL and the donation gates apply to the new layout.
findings.title: Threat model does not cover the new default-on encrypted SSD cache and full-state codec for a GLM model
